# Introduction

This guide shows you how to carry out meta analyses for six different types of data:<br>

-   **Continuous data** where there are mean and standard deviation values for both an experimental/treatment group and a control group;
-   **Binary data** where there are counts of binary events (*eg* success or failure, male or female, survival or death, heads or tails *etc*) in a treatment group and a control group;
-   **Correlations** where papers report the strength of a relationship between 2 variables;
-   Papers that report just a **single mean** and standard deviation as the result;
-   **Proportions**. For example, where the number of people out of a total respond in a particular way;
-   **Pre-calculated effect sizes**: if papers report effect sizes such as Hazard Ratios, Risk Ratios, Odds Ratios, or standardised mean differences, you can use this method.

To get started, you will need to load the following packages to R (open the box below):

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" collapse="true" title="Click to see packages to load (Copy and paste to Script editor)"}
```{r}
#| label: packages
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)
library(meta)
library(dmetar)
```

To be able to load `dmetar`, you must install it first from:<br> `devtools::install_github("MathiasHarrer/dmetar")`<br> <br>It needs \``` devtools` `` to have been installed already. <br>\``` dmetar` `` makes some aspects of meta-analysis easier in R. Once installed, you can load dmetar
:::
